name: Mitochondrial Oxidative Phosphorylation Disorder Due to Mitochondrial DNA Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of multisystem clinical features consistent with mitochondrial dysfunction including neurological and muscular symptoms
Demonstration of impaired oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activities in muscle or other tissues
Identification of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA mutations or deletions associated with oxidative phosphorylation defects
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers or cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficient fibers
Elevated lactate levels in blood or cerebrospinal fluid indicating mitochondrial dysfunction

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multisystem clinical features plus biochemical evidence of oxidative phosphorylation deficiency and confirmation of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA anomaly
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires integration of clinical, biochemical, histological, and genetic data.

pathognomonic.notes: Indicative of mitochondrial proliferation in muscle tissue
searchTerms: muscle biopsy showing ragged red fibers
abnormal muscle fibers with red staining

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cytochrome c oxidase (COX) deficient muscle fibers
searchTerms: muscle fibers lacking cytochrome c oxidase

pathognomonic.symptomName: Mitochondrial DNA deletions or point mutations detected

common.notes: Weakness of extraocular muscles causing ptosis and limited eye movement
Elevated lactate due to impaired oxidative metabolism
Peripheral nerve involvement causing sensory and motor deficits

occasional.notes: May occur due to central nervous system involvement
Cerebellar involvement leading to coordination deficits

rare.notes: Visual loss due to optic nerve involvement

laboratory: Elevated blood and CSF lactate and pyruvate levels
Abnormal oxidative phosphorylation enzyme activities in muscle biopsy
Elevated creatine kinase (CK) in some cases
imaging: Brain MRI showing stroke-like lesions or basal ganglia abnormalities
Muscle MRI may show fatty infiltration or atrophy
genetic: Detection of pathogenic mitochondrial DNA point mutations, deletions, or rearrangements
Heteroplasmy levels correlating with disease severity
other: Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX-negative fibers

distinguishingFeatures: Primarily optic neuropathy with acute/subacute vision loss
Typically lacks multisystem involvement seen in mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation disorder
Onset before age 20 with progressive external ophthalmoplegia and pigmentary retinopathy
Presence of cardiac conduction defects and cerebellar ataxia

redFlags: Rapidly progressive external ophthalmoplegia with multisystem involvement
Elevated lactate in blood or CSF without other metabolic causes
Muscle biopsy showing ragged-red fibers and COX deficiency
references: DiMauro S, Schon EA. Mitochondrial respiratory-chain diseases. N Engl J Med. 2003 Jun 19;348(26):2656-68.
